To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solar peculiar motion is 5.0 km s-1 toward Galactic rotation, the LSR speed is 270 ± 5 km s-2, the disk velocity ellipsoid points toward the Galactic nucleus, the thick disk velocity ellipsoid shows a rather strong negative velocity gradient, and there might be substructure in the disk proper motions at the brighter magnitudes.

the Galactic structure and kinematics are consistent with a high LSR rotation speed of 270 ± 20 km s-1 and that a solar peculiar motion is required in order to explain the kinematics of the disk stars in this part of the Galaxy.

the absolute proper motions in U, V, and W are best described by a Galactic model that has a solar peculiar motion in the V-component of 5 ± 1 km s-1 (pointing in a direction of Galactic rotation) and a high LSR velocity of 270 ± 20 km s-1.
